title: U.S. Senate (special) · Ohio

context.text: This is a special election to fill the remainder of the U.S. Senate term won by J.D. Vance in 2022. Gov. Mike DeWine appointed Jon Husted to the seat on January 17, 2025 after Vance became vice president. The winner serves the rest of the term, through January 2029.
Sherrod Brown defeated Ron Kincaid in the Democratic primary on May 5, 2026, 89.4% to 10.6%. Jon Husted was unopposed in the Republican primary. Bill Redpath was unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Jon Husted
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Husted is the incumbent, appointed to the Senate by Gov. Mike DeWine in January 2025 to replace J.D. Vance. He previously served as Ohio's lieutenant governor (2019-2025), secretary of state (2011-2019), a state senator (2009-2011), and a state representative including as House speaker (2001-2009).

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in education (1982) and a master's degree in communications (1989) from the University of Dayton.
Before elected office, worked as Vice President of Business and Economic Development at the Dayton Area Chamber of Commerce.
Served as Ohio House speaker from 2005 to 2009 and later as Ohio Secretary of State (2011-2019) and Lieutenant Governor (2019-2025) under Gov. Mike DeWine.

priorities.text: Campaigned on his record in state government, citing a 'conservative, balanced budget with the largest tax cut in Ohio history' as House speaker and economic development efforts as lieutenant governor.

Says he has worked in the Senate to pass an 'America First agenda,' including 'securing our border and adding more agents, delivering the largest tax cut in American history for middle class families, eliminating taxes on tips and overtime, empowering parents so they can keep their children safe online.'
priorities.quote: securing our border and adding more agents, delivering the largest tax cut in American history for middle class families, eliminating taxes on tips and overtime, empowering parents so they can can keep their children safe online.

record.text: Appointed by Gov. Mike DeWine to the U.S. Senate on January 17, 2025, to fill the seat vacated by J.D. Vance.
Serves on the Senate Special Committee on Aging, Committee on Environment and Public Works, Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions, and Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
As Ohio House speaker (2005-2009), signed off on a state budget he describes as including 'the largest tax cut in Ohio history.'

candidates.name: Sherrod Brown
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, 89.4% to 10.6%

summary.text: Brown is a former three-term U.S. senator who lost re-election to Bernie Moreno in 2024. He previously served in the U.S. House (1993-2007), as Ohio Secretary of State (1983-1991), and in the Ohio House (1975-1982).

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in Russian studies from Yale University (1974) and a graduate degree in education from Ohio State University (1981).
Was a faculty member at Ohio State University before holding public office.
Lost re-election to the Senate to Bernie Moreno in 2024, 50.1% to 46.5%.

priorities.text: Campaign website states he 'led the charge to make sure over 100,000 Ohioans got the retirement they were owed' and 'successfully fought to cap the cost of insulin and reduce the price of other prescription drugs for Ohio seniors.'
priorities.quote: led the charge to make sure over 100,000 Ohioans got the retirement they were owed

priorities.text: Criticizes Republican economic policy, saying tariffs and other measures are 'increasing prices and threatening the survival of small businesses all across our state.'
priorities.quote: Their reckless tariffs and economic chaos are increasing prices and threatening the survival of small businesses all across our state.

positions.summary: Criticizes Republicans' tariff policy as raising prices and hurting small businesses.
positions.quote: Their reckless tariffs and economic chaos are increasing prices and threatening the survival of small businesses all across our state.

positions.summary: Says Republicans are 'kicking 490,000 hardworking Ohioans off their coverage' while raising drug prices, framing health-coverage access as a priority.
positions.quote: Instead of lowering the cost of health care, they're raising drug prices on seniors and kicking 490,000 hardworking Ohioans off their coverage.

candidates.name: Bill Redpath
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Libertarian primary unopposed

summary.text: Redpath is a Libertarian Party activist and retired business-valuation consultant from Perrysburg, Ohio, who has been a nine-time Libertarian candidate for public office and chaired the Libertarian National Committee from 2006 to 2010.

background.text: Earned a BA in economics and political science from Indiana University and an MBA from the University of Chicago.
Had a 38-year career in business valuation, specializing in media and telecommunications, including at BIA Advisory Services and Summit Ridge Group.

priorities.text: Supports reducing federal spending, warning of a possible debt crisis, and wants the Federal Reserve to focus solely on an inflation target rather than a 'dual mandate' that also targets employment.
Calls for repealing all tariffs, including those imposed under the Trump administration, in favor of 'unilateral free trade.'
priorities.quote: Repeal not just Trump's tariffs, but all tariffs. I support a policy of unilateral free trade, which is a pro-consumer trade policy.

priorities.text: Supports open immigration except for criminals, terrorists, and others who would pose a danger, and opposes U.S. military interventionism.

positions.summary: Wants to repeal all tariffs, including those imposed under the Trump administration, favoring unilateral free trade.
positions.quote: Repeal not just Trump's tariffs, but all tariffs. I support a policy of unilateral free trade, which is a pro-consumer trade policy.

positions.summary: Supports open immigration, opposing broad enforcement/deportation, with exceptions only for criminals, terrorists, and those who would harm others.
positions.quote: All immigration should be allowed except for a handful of people who fall into the categories of criminals, terrorists, the seriously ill, or others who would harm the life, liberty, and property of people here.

positions.summary: Opposes the U.S. 'special relationship' with Israel's government, saying Israel should be treated like any other allied nation.
positions.quote: The "special relationship" with the government of Israel only leads the US into problems. We should treat Israel like any other allied nation.

candidates.name: Gregory Levy

summary.text: Levy is an independent candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for U.S. Senate. Ballotpedia's campaign-finance tracker shows he had raised $80,348 and spent $56,132 as of June 30, 2026, but no campaign website, biography, or policy statements were found.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, biography, or public policy statements found for Gregory Levy beyond Ballotpedia's fundraising figures. Could not confirm additional background.
